claims.text: Replacing EAM references with machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method is applicable to both solid and liquid states near the alloys' high melting temperatures.
Machine-learned interatomic potentials can capture the complex atomic interactions present in ab initio liquid simulations.
Machine-learned interatomic potentials can capture the atomic configurations present in ab initio liquid simulations.
EAM references inadequately represent the configurations sampled by ab initio liquids.
The simpler functional forms of EAM references cause their inadequate representation of ab initio-liquid configurations.
Improved representation of liquid-state configurations will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce more accurate free-energy calculations.
The applicable alloys contain at least five principal elements.
The applicable temperature range is 0.9–1.1 times the alloy melting temperature.
The hypothesis does not apply to alloys with fewer than five principal elements or at temperatures significantly below the melting point.
A direct comparison of thermodynamic integration using the machine-learned reference and an EAM reference can test the hypothesis.
Failure to improve phase-space overlap or reduce path mismatch relative to the EAM reference would falsify the hypothesis.
